steps.say: Revised Atlanta splits interstitial oedematous disease from necrotising pancreatitis. Organ failure under forty eight hours marks moderately severe disease, while persistent failure marks severe disease. The clock on organ failure writes the severity label.
steps.tx: **Revised Atlanta** classifies interstitial oedematous against **necrotising pancreatitis**, with organ failure under **48** hours marking moderately severe and persistent failure marking severe pancreatitis. Local complications of collections and necrosis layer onto this physiologic grading, and infected necrosis upgrades every category. Score severity daily, since moderately severe disease can still deteriorate into persistent failure.

vis.alt: Pancreatic necrosis with walled-off necrosis, fat saponification, main duct and CT inset of acute pancreatitis.
vis.caption: Necrosis, walled-off necrosis and saponification. Image: StewardMD.

steps.say: Gallstones and alcohol cause eighty percent of attacks, with triglycerides over a thousand and calcium over ten as metabolic triggers. Biliary cases need same admission cholecystectomy once settled. Check lipids and calcium in every first attack.
steps.tx: Gallstones and alcohol cause **80** percent of attacks, with **triglycerides** over **1000** mg per dL and calcium over **10** mg per dL as metabolic triggers needing **same-admission cholecystectomy** for biliary cases. Hypertriglyceride pancreatitis needs insulin with heparin or plasmapheresis plus fibrates, while hypercalcaemia points to parathyroid disease. Remove the gallbladder on the same admission after biliary attacks, since interval attacks recur fast.

steps.say: Contrast CT at seventy two to ninety six hours stages necrosis and detects gas in infected necrosis. Early CT underestimates necrosis and stays reserved for diagnostic doubt. Gas bubbles in dead pancreas mean infection until proven otherwise.
steps.tx: **Contrast CT** at **72** to **96** hours stages necrosis and detects gas in **infected necrosis**, while early CT underestimates necrosis and is reserved for diagnostic doubt. Non-enhancement maps dead parenchyma, and extraluminal gas or a positive needle aspirate proves infection. Repeat imaging only for deterioration, since scheduled rescans add contrast load without changing step-up timing.

steps.say: Infected necrosis with gas, positive culture or persistent sepsis beyond four weeks follows the PANTER step up. Drain first, percutaneously in PANTER or endoscopically in TENSION, then debride by the retroperitoneal route or endoscopically only if drainage fails. Each step up only follows failure of the one below.
steps.tx: Infected necrosis with gas, positive culture or persistent sepsis beyond **4** weeks follows the PANTER and TENSION **step-up**: percutaneous or endoscopic transluminal drainage first, then necrosectomy (video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement in PANTER, endoscopic in TENSION) only if drainage fails. Delaying intervention lets collections wall off and improves endoscopic success, while early open necrosectomy bleeds and fistulises. Antibiotics alone suit sepsis without gas or deterioration, with escalation driven by cultures and clinical course.

points: Drain first, then debride if needed
left.title: Step-up (PANTER/TENSION)

steps.say: Walled-off necrosis after four weeks with obstruction, pain or infection gets endoscopic cystgastrostomy with lumen apposing metal stents rather than open surgery. The stent creates a wide mouth for necrosectomy through the stomach. Mature walls make this safe.
steps.tx: **Walled-off necrosis** after **4** weeks with obstruction, pain or infection gets endoscopic **cystgastrostomy** with **lumen-apposing stent** rather than open surgery. The short wide stent apposes stomach to cavity for direct necrosectomy sessions, and double pigtails through it keep the track open. Collections without symptoms simply watch, since half resolve and intervention risks introducing infection.

vis.alt: Transgastric metal stent draining walled-off necrosis with fibrous capsule and necrotic debris into the stomach.
vis.caption: Lumen-apposing stent into walled-off necrosis. Image: StewardMD.

steps.say: Abdominal compartment syndrome kills silently in severe pancreatitis with massive fluid resuscitation. Bladder pressure over twenty with new organ failure needs decompressive laparotomy, with percutaneous drainage tried first when collections dominate. Measure bladder pressure in every tense abdomen.
steps.tx: Abdominal compartment syndrome with **bladder pressure** over **20** mmHg plus organ failure needs decompressive laparotomy, and percutaneous drainage is tried first when collections dominate. Tense distension with oliguria, rising airway pressures and falling cardiac output complete the picture. Medical measures of nasogastric suction, diuresis and neuromuscular blockade precede the knife, but delay beyond established failure kills bowel.

steps.say: Feed the gut early through a nasojejunal tube within forty eight hours. Enteral feeding preserves the gut barrier and cuts infection, while prophylactic antibiotics and probiotics do not prevent infected necrosis. Starving the gut translocates bacteria.
steps.tx: **Enteral feeding** within **48** hours through **nasojejunal** tube preserves **gut barrier** and cuts infection, while prophylactic antibiotics and probiotics do not prevent infected necrosis. Post-pyloric feeding past the inflamed duodenum avoids stimulation, and trickle feeds advance as pain and ileus allow. Parenteral nutrition waits for failed enteral access or prolonged ileus, never as the first choice.

steps.say: Cholangitis with biliary pancreatitis needs ERCP within twenty four hours, while mere obstruction without cholangitis waits for the attack to settle. Fever with jaundice and pain means infected bile under pressure. Drain infected ducts urgently, leave clean obstruction alone.
steps.tx: **Biliary pancreatitis** with cholangitis needs **urgent ERCP** within **24** hours, while mere biliary obstruction without **cholangitis** waits for the attack to settle before elective clearance. Charcot fever with jaundice marks infected obstruction demanding sphincterotomy, whereas a quiet dilated duct clears after the inflammation passes. Same-admission cholecystectomy then prevents the next attack.
